speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Since you presented with an episode of loss of consciousness, I need to ask you a few specific questions to determine the cause. How long were you unconscious, and did you lose any control of your bladder or bowels during the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: TIA (Transient Ischemic Attack) secondary to cervical artery dissection or orthostatic hypotension. Given the timing "immediately after micturating," I suspect orthostatic hypotension or vasovagal syncope; however, the lack of post-ictal confusion makes epilepsy unlikely. REQUEST TEST: Blood_pressure_measurement (supine and standing), ECG, and Head_CT_scan to rule out intracranial hemorrhage or large vessel occlusion.
